name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt just above 5.2% on 12 Nov after two-month lows; 2056 gilt sold at 5.54% on 10 Nov with solid demand
state: The 10-year gilt yield was just above 5.2% on 12 Nov, rebounding from its lowest in more than two months, as markets priced another Bank of England rise by year-end (InstaForex). It had fallen towards 5.1% on 6 Nov after the BoE raised rates (Trading Economics). The DMO sold £1bn of the 2056 gilt on 10 Nov at an average 5.54% yield, covered 3.75 times with a 0.3bp tail, an orderly result (DMO). Watch is kept because long yields remain near multi-decade highs.
for_you: Higher long-term gilt yields feed through to mortgage rates, annuity rates and government borrowing costs. Conditions are steadier than in October, with recent auctions well covered.
rubric_hit: Watch: 30y-area yields near multi-decade highs (2056 gilt 5.54%, 10 Nov); 10y move < 40bp in a month; auctions orderly

sources.title: InstaForex — UK gilt yields rise from over two-month lows
Trading Economics — UK gilt yields fall as flight to safety offsets hawkish BoE stance

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
